title: What running a high-volume assembly line involves
why: Adding capacity means working the bottleneck; sampling-based QA lets some defects through; labor balancing and forklift accidents can stall whole lines.

title: Using RSS feeds to replace social platforms
why: hnrss.org provides feeds for HN replies, Ask HN and Show HN; RSS also tracks CVEs, distro security notices and SourceHut commits.

title: DigitalOcean's public response to an abuse incident
why: Corporate statement with a timeline of monitoring alerts and customer contact; it argues a position rather than teaching a technique.

title: Why Hollywood's formula-based studio model fails
why: Films are one-off bets, not widgets; a Corman-style system of many cheap projects with young talent limits risk per project.

title: Bitcoin's fixed economics as governance without consent
why: Argues that built-in monetary assumptions constrain users who cannot vote on them; a values argument rather than an explanation.

title: Why Microsoft shifted Windows testing to telemetry
why: After dedicated testers were cut in 2014, Microsoft relied on developer tests, beta programs and telemetry; crash dumps find bugs testing misses.

title: Why submenus open after a deliberate delay
why: Apple's 1995 guidelines explain the submenu delay: it stops pointer sweeps across menus from opening submenus accidentally.

title: Why China's maps use GCJ-02 coordinates
why: China requires the obfuscated GCJ-02 offset of WGS-84, so satellite overlays misalign by 50-500m unless coordinates are converted.

title: Why early 4K monitors needed display-driver hacks
why: HDMI and DisplayPort 1.2 couldn't drive 4K at 60Hz natively; drivers faked it as two tiles, causing window-spanning problems on Linux and ChromeOS.

title: Opinion on manned fighter jets and drones
why: Unqualified opinion that manned fighters are obsolete; argues from cost and timelines without technical analysis.

title: Why repair shops see fewer iPhone upgrades
why: Visible plan costs and cheap 30-minute screen repairs let owners keep old iPhones, which depresses upgrade demand.

title: How a 10-line APL program beat a 300-line BASIC port
why: Translating BASIC line by line keeps its structure; rethinking the problem with array operations shrank the program dramatically.

title: What made Agile work versus how it degraded
why: Honest estimates, team-only standups and real demos worked; public boards and managers turned them into self-promotion and deadline pressure.

title: Critique of a booking-logistics startup
why: Argues talent is wasted on airport pickup; a values opinion about what startups should solve.

title: Four design basics every engineer should learn
why: Visual hierarchy, basic typography, UX thinking from Don't Make Me Think, and what colors signal for alerts and branding.

title: Leaderboard of em dash use before and after ChatGPT
why: A data leaderboard with a caveat that dash usage doesn't prove ChatGPT use; it teaches little on its own.

title: Why Opera's all-in-one design was hard to recreate
why: Opera packed mail, feeds, torrents and notes into a roughly 5MB native browser; web-tech rebuilds of that breadth are bulkier and slower.

title: Argument that trust is a feature, not a bug
why: A philosophical position against trust-eliminating technology; it argues values rather than explaining a mechanism.

title: Family cookbook story and restaurant tips
why: Personal anecdote and recommendations about San Antonio food, with no transferable technical lesson.

title: Personal case for suburban living
why: Personal lifestyle preference and reflection; no explanatory content.

title: Canadian border agents demanding a phone password
why: Personal account of an intrusive search; it recounts an experience rather than explaining a practice.

title: Opinion on ex-employees competing with employers
why: Opinion about business rivalry and ex-employee startups without substantive explanation.

title: Argument against web bloat over faster protocols
why: Persuasive opinion that page weight, not transport speed, makes sites slow; argues rather than explains a mechanism.

title: List of Windows 10 frustrations
why: A complaint list of hardware and OS bugs with no general lesson beyond personal troubleshooting.

title: Argument about the Google memo controversy
why: Political argument about a company memo and its firing; no technical learning.

title: How physics replicates results without rerunning experiments
why: Big experiments can't be repeated, so physics relies on cross-checks between detectors, many observations and systematic-bias hunts.

title: Hiring advertisement for a game designer
why: A job advertisement with no explanatory content.

title: Personal story about Shazam finding a song
why: Nostalgic personal anecdote about a music app; no transferable lesson.

title: Matrix's plans to fix Riot and Synapse performance
why: Lazy-loading room members cuts RAM 3x-20x; cross-signing ends repeated device verification; Synapse hot paths move toward constant cost per room size.

title: Why Vista's reputation suffered: drivers and SuperFetch
why: Vista exposed poor vendor drivers, and aggressive SuperFetch prefetching overloaded spinning disks with random reads, slowing the first minutes after boot.

title: Why Tailscale's iOS client can't be open sourced
why: Network Extension entitlements are tied to Apple's corporate account, so even open source code wouldn't run without it; macOS dev setup is fragile.

title: How ReadyReturn pre-filled taxes and why it stalled
why: Pre-filled returns using data the government already holds won near-universal approval in tests, but partly lobbying by tax software firms stopped it.

title: How Apple rejected an app over account requirements
why: Apple rejected a subscription app a week before launch for requiring email accounts for in-app purchase, despite prior approvals.

title: Why FISA courts differ from Article III courts
why: FISC is a congressional creation without lifetime tenure or adversarial hearings, so claims about Roberts' lifetime surveillance power misread the structure.

title: Argument for keeping manual car controls
why: Use-case argument for manual controls for parking and odd maneuvers; opinion about product design rather than technical knowledge.

title: Analysis of Intel's cloud pricing pressure
why: Market speculation about ARM instances and chip margins; opinion without verified expertise.

title: Personal experience of sleep-onset imagery
why: Personal anecdote about observing the transition to sleep; no explained mechanism or actionable lesson.

title: Why FoldingCoin gave up decentralization
why: Critique showing a useful proof-of-work tied to an external network makes distribution depend on one trusted party; argument rather than a tutorial.

title: Using arbitration and state UDAP laws to win claims
why: State deceptive-practices laws can treble damages and award attorney fees, which pressures companies toward early settlements.

title: Why software estimates should admit uncertainty
why: Give ranges and timeboxes, naming unknowns like unfamiliar APIs or bug hunts, instead of dates you then miss.

title: How game rules distorted high school debate
why: Treating dropped arguments as conceded rewarded fast spreading; any scored competition tends to optimize for the rules over the activity's purpose.

title: Defense of the typical hiring process
why: Opinion that people who fail interviews blame the process; argument rather than explanation.

title: Why engagement experiments can hurt long-term health
why: Teams choose winners on short-term engagement while long-term holdout groups go unreviewed, so incentives reward immediate-metric features.

title: Personal case for finishing a degree
why: Personal reasons and opinion on college; anecdotal advice without a transferable technical lesson.

title: Ethics of accepting fund investors
why: Anecdotes and questions about investor ethics; opinion without a clear explanatory lesson.

title: Why mature markets differentiate through marketing
why: In mature markets products are technically equivalent, so brands differentiate on positioning and image; engineers often overlook that lever.

title: Complaints about noisy coworking spaces
why: Personal complaints about noise and social awkwardness in shared offices; no transferable lesson.

title: How FRAND licensing differs from ordinary patents
why: Standards-essential patents must be licensed on fair, reasonable, non-discriminatory terms, so Apple's suit enforced those terms rather than claiming feature patents.

title: Why version control fails for law documents
why: Conflicting legislative branches can't simply be merged; systems keep parallel versions until a court or legislature decides, which takes years.

title: Essay on who gains from automation
why: Cultural and political opinion about work and basic income; argues values rather than explaining technical content.

title: Filter rules that neutralize YouTube anti-adblock checks
why: A list of uBlock-style rules using set and aeld scriptlets to neutralize anti-adblock checks and remove on-screen annoyances; practical but terse.

title: Why origin IP allowlisting alone isn't enough
why: Origins must also check the Host header or use authenticated origin pulls or Argo Tunnel, since CDNs cannot verify origin ownership.

title: Ex-Marine's path into programming
why: Personal career narrative about CS study and the GI Bill; no transferable technical lesson.

title: Argument that side projects are realistic
why: Opinion countering a common excuse; argues priorities rather than teaching a technique.

title: A career arc from design patterns back to simple code
why: After years of factories and DI layers that multiplied files per change, minimal code with few core files proved far more productive.

title: Why Google keeps Maps and Play protocols proprietary
why: Map data licenses restrict distribution, Play needs anti-fraud controls, and a single controlled client lets Google change protocols freely.

title: Essay critiquing 'trust the science'
why: Opinion that science cannot settle economic value trade-offs; a political essay rather than technical explanation.

title: HATEOAS describes how websites already work
why: Following links and submitting forms drives state changes in a browser, which is Fielding's hypermedia-as-engine-of-state idea; most REST APIs omit it.

why: Speculative financial commentary about cash burn and pricing; predictions rather than verifiable explanation.

why: Personal feelings about community norms; opinion without a technical lesson.

why: Personal reflection and advice on social life; no technical or historical lesson.

title: Parent objects to four-hour coding tests
why: Personal schedule and opinion about hiring assignments; context-bound rather than instructive.

title: Why Bitcoin transaction IDs can change
why: Transaction IDs derive from malleable content, so the correct way to find a sent transaction is scanning history for matching parameters.

title: Practical Haskell performance rules for large data
why: Avoid thunk buildup in long loops, use Text and ByteString instead of String, prefer Vector for finite data, and stream large inputs.

title: Essay defending science fiction as thought experiments
why: Opinion piece praising sci-fi as concept simulation; argues for a genre rather than teaching a method.

title: Argument on what counts as a better society
why: Philosophical argument about utopias and capitalism; opinion without explanatory content.

title: How to charge Li-ion batteries for longer life
why: Li-ion cells degrade faster at high state of charge, so keeping them around 50-80% and avoiding deep cycles extends battery life.

title: Personal SQL formatting conventions
why: Style preferences with brief reasoning; useful to some readers but mostly taste rather than knowledge.

title: Defense of unpaid take-home interviews
why: Opinion on interview effort versus pay; argues rather than explains.

title: Company clarification on droplet snapshots and scrubbing

why: Personal question seeking advice; no explanatory content about CRDTs themselves.
